evals.prompt: Audit the SEO on this Astro site and propose the first changes.
evals.expected_behavior: Confirms Astro config/site origin first, audits technical SEO surfaces, and separates metadata copy review from implementation.
assertions: Reads astro.config/package setup before proposing canonical or sitemap work
Checks metadata, structured data, OG, sitemap/robots/RSS, and indexing surfaces
Mentions writing-and-editing only for generated short strings or prose follow-up

evals.prompt: Check these title tags and descriptions for truncation and rewrite weak ones.
evals.expected_behavior: Routes the copy-only task away from Astro technical SEO.
assertions: Does not treat copy-only metadata review as an Astro SEO implementation task
Recommends writing-and-editing metadata-audit mode

evals.expected_behavior: Treats the missing production site origin as blocking before canonical, sitemap, or OG URL work.
assertions: Flags the missing or local-only site value as a blocking prerequisite
Does not proceed as if canonical, sitemap, or OG URLs were already valid
Points the fix at the site field in astro.config
Explains which outputs depend on the origin (canonicals, sitemaps, OG URLs)

evals.prompt: Our Astro site already has hand-rolled canonical tags, a working sitemap integration, and valid Article JSON-LD in the blog layout. A teammate wants to rip it out and install @jdevalk/astro-seo-graph. Should we?
evals.expected_behavior: Audits the existing setup first and does not assume every finding requires replacing the stack.
assertions: Audits what the existing hand-rolled setup already covers before recommending replacement
Does not recommend wholesale replacement purely because the package exists
Recommends the package only for gaps it materially simplifies
Keeps the answer tied to the described Astro files rather than generic SEO advice

evals.prompt: This Astro project has no head metadata component, no JSON-LD, no IndexNow, and no build-time SEO validation. Nothing SEO-related is installed yet. What should we set up?
evals.expected_behavior: Recommends installing the Astro SEO package as the default spine and names what it covers.
assertions: Recommends installing @jdevalk/astro-seo-graph as the default spine
Names the covered surfaces such as head metadata, schema, IndexNow, redirects, and build-time validation
Branches on install when missing rather than upgrading
Mentions validating with astro check or the project build

evals.prompt: Our Astro site is statically built and meta tags are missing on some pages. I was thinking of switching to SSR with a client-only head component to fix it. Does that sound right?
evals.expected_behavior: Rejects adding SSR or client hydration to solve an SEO problem a static build already handles.
assertions: Rejects switching to SSR or client hydration for this problem
Explains that a static Astro build can emit the metadata at build time
Points at the head layout, component, or config as the correct fix location
Does not accept the proposed approach

evals.prompt: Our Astro config declares i18n with 'en' and 'de' locales, and content lives in src/content/<locale>/. We rank only in English. Set up the locale alternates correctly.
evals.expected_behavior: Reads the i18n config and wires hreflang alternates plus per-locale canonicals.
assertions: Checks the Astro i18n configuration before proposing changes
Covers hreflang alternate links for each declared locale
Uses per-locale canonical URLs rather than one shared canonical
Does not invent locales beyond the two declared

evals.prompt: Our Astro blog layout outputs title, description, and date frontmatter but no structured data. Add Article structured data properly.
evals.expected_behavior: Adds JSON-LD built from real frontmatter fields in the blog layout rather than hardcoded text.
assertions: Adds JSON-LD structured data in the layout or head output
Derives values from the existing title, description, and date frontmatter
Uses an appropriate schema type such as BlogPosting or Article
Does not hardcode placeholder content into the structured data

evals.prompt: We want a unique Open Graph image per blog post on a statically built Astro site. What is the right implementation path?
evals.expected_behavior: Proposes build-time OG image generation with absolute URLs derived from the site origin.
assertions: Proposes build-time OG image generation rather than runtime SSR
Notes that OG image URLs must be absolute and depend on the configured site origin
Covers both og:image and the Twitter card metadata
Keeps the recommendation tied to Astro routes or the existing SEO library

evals.prompt: Search Console reports duplicate content across our paginated blog index: /blog, /blog/2, /blog/3. Each page currently emits the same canonical pointing at /blog. Fix the canonical strategy.
evals.expected_behavior: Gives each paginated page its own canonical and avoids collapsing them onto page one.
assertions: Points out that the shared canonical is the cause of the duplicate report
Gives each paginated page a self-referential canonical
Does not keep all pages pointing at /blog
Mentions the crawl or indexing surface rather than only rewriting copy

evals.prompt: Set up IndexNow for our Astro site so new posts get submitted automatically.
evals.expected_behavior: Covers the package path plus the manual key and verification work the repo cannot automate.
assertions: Recommends the Astro SEO package as the implementation path where appropriate
Calls out the manual setup the repo cannot automate, such as key management and verification
Describes validating the generated key file or submission output
Does not claim full automation of search engine registration

evals.prompt: Our CI runs `npm run build || true` and the build prints SEO validation warnings about missing descriptions. Fix the pipeline so those warnings actually matter.
evals.expected_behavior: Surfaces build-time SEO warnings explicitly instead of letting a passing build hide them.
assertions: Removes or replaces the swallow-everything pattern so failures surface
Runs the project build or astro check as the validation step
States that SEO validation warnings should be visible in CI, not hidden behind a passing build
Ties the fix to the CI or build script rather than to metadata copy

evals.prompt: We publish an RSS feed at /rss.xml but our head does not reference it. Wire up feed discovery correctly.
evals.expected_behavior: Adds RSS autodiscovery alternate links with absolute URLs derived from the site origin.
assertions: Adds a link rel=alternate element for the RSS feed
Uses the correct feed MIME type such as application/rss+xml
Ensures the feed URL is absolute from the configured site origin
Verifies the feed path matches the published route

evals.prompt: An AI crawler audit flagged that our Astro docs site exposes nothing for agent discovery. What should we add?
evals.expected_behavior: Covers the agent-discovery surfaces the skill owns: schema endpoints, schema maps, llms.txt, and markdown alternates.
assertions: Covers agent-discovery surfaces such as llms.txt, schema endpoints or schema maps, and markdown alternates
Ties each surface to a real Astro route or generated file
Distinguishes these surfaces from classic search-engine metadata
Recommends validating the generated routes or files

evals.prompt: Audit the SEO of our Next.js marketing site and fix the metadata setup.
evals.expected_behavior: Declines the Astro-specific workflow because the project is not Astro.
assertions: States that the Astro SEO workflow does not apply to a Next.js project
Does not prescribe Astro config, integrations, or Astro-specific recipes
Offers generic or framework-appropriate guidance instead of forcing the Astro path

evals.prompt: Give me a content marketing strategy for my personal blog — what topics should I write about to grow traffic?
evals.expected_behavior: Routes away from the Astro SEO implementation skill because there is no repository or technical SEO work.
assertions: Does not treat the request as Astro SEO implementation work
States that the task is broad content strategy rather than technical SEO
Does not invent repository files or Astro config to modify

evals.prompt: Audit the SEO on this Astro site and propose the first changes.
evals.expected_behavior: Confirms this is an Astro site and reads astro.config.* (site origin, adapter, i18n) before proposing any canonical, sitemap, or OG change, treating a missing or local-only site config as blocking.
assertions: Reads astro.config.* and confirms the production site origin before proposing canonical/sitemap/OG work
Checks package.json and whether @jdevalk/astro-seo-graph is already installed
Treats a missing or local-only site config as a blocking issue rather than proceeding anyway

evals.prompt: Our Astro site already has a working hand-rolled SEO setup with good metadata and a sitemap, but we're missing structured data and llms.txt. Fix the gaps.
evals.expected_behavior: Recommends the smallest coherent implementation path: preserve the existing hand-rolled setup where it already works and add only the missing structured data and llms.txt pieces, rather than replacing the whole stack.
assertions: Does not propose replacing the existing SEO stack when it already satisfies the working requirements
Scopes the implementation to the actually missing pieces (structured data, llms.txt)
Only suggests @jdevalk/astro-seo-graph if it materially simplifies the missing pieces, not as a default rip-and-replace
